mw-bark-badger.concept: A badger seen face-on. Its square head and body is an inner-TTBB piece with peg knobs: the N tab is a grass tuft on its crown, the E tab is a bark sleeve held out to share the coat, and the W and S blanks are cut into the oak-bark cloak (the S blank sits between its paws). The grey fur, sand-coloured face stripe and grass green come from cell 6-6 (gravel, path, grass); the bark brown and the maple-gold leaf brooch come from the picture's oak.
mw-bark-badger.name: pass
mw-bark-badger.notes: The bark coat reads only as a plain brown cloak: the furrow texture is faint at 64 px and almost gone at 36 px, so "bark" relies on colour. The link to the cell is in the colours only (grass, path, gravel), with no strong motif from it, and the grass tuft tab looks a bit like a green cap. Files are in /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mw-bark-badger.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mw-bark-badger{,-36,-preview}.png.

mh-husk-hopper.concept: A side-view grasshopper that is a corner piece. Its head is the round tab on the right with two antennae, a round blank is cut into its rump, and the top and bottom sides are flat. The body is a green corn husk opened on a yellow cob belly, with a big pale folded hind leg whose knee pokes above the top edge. It stands on a strip of furrowed brown soil, using the stalk green, cob yellow and furrow brown of cell 2-6.
mh-husk-hopper.name: partial
mh-husk-hopper.notes: Grasshopper still only reads as "partial". The head on the tab, with no mouth, could pass for a snail or caterpillar, and the hind leg is the main cue. At 36 px that leg turns into a pale diagonal stripe, so a stranger may only say "green bug".

ss-palm-fidget.concept: A little coconut palm that is also an edge piece. The flat side is a sandy base, the top keyhole tab is a sprouting coconut rising out of the green frond crown, and keyhole blanks cut into the left and right of the tan ringed trunk. Fronds droop over the top corners and arch up beside the tab, and a face sits on the trunk.
ss-palm-fidget.name: partial
ss-palm-fidget.notes: The trunk is a wide square block, so the pal reads more as a palm crown on a stump or potted plant than as a slim palm tree. The cell (5-0) is mostly a seagull wing on sky, so only its tan and brown (trunk and rings) and sky blue (breeze marks) carry over. The palm, coconut and sand motif comes from the wider picture, not the cell. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ss-palm-fidget.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-palm-fidget.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-palm-fidget-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-palm-fidget-preview.png

mh-golden-ring.concept: A golden maize harvest wreath (a ring of corn kernels with a hole in the middle) that is an inner-BBBB piece: round blanks on all four sides, a rounded-square body, a wood-brown lip round the ring's hole (which doubles as the creature's open "O" mouth), cream husk leaves and a red flower tucked at the upper left. The gold, cream plaster, wood brown and red flower all come from cell 6-4.
mh-golden-ring.name: partial
mh-golden-ring.notes: The kernel texture says "corn" well at 64 px, but a stranger might call it a golden donut or cookie ring rather than a harvest wreath, especially at 36 px where the husk leaves shrink to a speck. The cell is mostly cream plaster and fountain, so the cream, brown and red picture link is weaker than the gold corn link from the wider Maize Hollow picture, and I left out the teal. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mh-golden-ring.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mh-golden-ring.png, mh-golden-ring-36.png and mh-golden-ring-preview.png. Both sizes pass the checks (alpha 0/255 only, no black, 17 and 16 colours).

ss-coral-cuff.concept: A square block of pink reef coral (inner-TTTT, double). The N, W and E double tabs are pale forked staghorn branch tips, and round coral fingers break out past the top corners. The S tab and the lower third are the teal sea 'cuff' from cell 8-3, topped by a cream foam/sail line. Cream polyps are dotted over the coral and the face sits on it.
ss-coral-cuff.name: partial
ss-coral-cuff.notes: It reads very clearly as a puzzle piece, but 'coral' only half reads. Out of context, the double-lobed pale tabs could pass for bones, and the branching inside the body is soft at 36 px. The cell is only teal water and a cream sail, so the coral pink comes from the shells on the beach in the wider picture, not from the cell.

ss-tide-tuck.concept: A sand crab tucked into the beach as a wave laps in, made as an inner-TTTB round piece. The N blank is the dip in its shell between the two eye bumps, the W and E tabs are notched pincer claws, and the S tab is a heap of sand. Brown and sand colours come from cell 3-5, and a teal and foam wave line comes from the picture's sea.
ss-tide-tuck.name: partial
ss-tide-tuck.notes: It reads more as a cute crab-like blob than a clear crab. There are no legs and the shell is a square block. The claw tabs are round knobs with a small notch, so at 36 px they can look like little hands rather than pincers. The grey-tan driftwood colour from the cell barely shows. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ss-tide-tuck.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-tide-tuck.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-tide-tuck-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-tide-tuck-preview.png.

ss-lagoon-loop.concept: A cream-and-coral life ring (the "loop") built as a rounded inner-BBBB piece. Each side has a keyhole blank cut in, coral bands run on the diagonals, and turquoise lagoon water fills the hole and forms a winking face. Colours are the cell's lagoon teal, cream sail and coral stripe.
ss-lagoon-loop.name: partial
ss-lagoon-loop.notes: The four deep blanks give the ring a squarish, four-lobed outline, so a stranger may first see a puzzle piece or a cross with a face rather than a life ring. The diagonal coral bands are what make it a life ring. At 36 px the keyhole flare is hard to tell from a round blank, and the wink is only a few pixels. Script: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ss-lagoon-loop.py. Outputs: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ss-lagoon-loop.png, ss-lagoon-loop-36.png, ss-lagoon-loop-preview.png.

rr-kapok-nook.concept: A kapok tree trunk that is also a corner piece and a little house. The left side and bottom are flat (the trunk's side and the ground). The round tab on top is the leafy crown, with a white kapok-fluff dot, and the round blank on the right bites into the bark. On the front are an arched wooden door, a round yellow window, a red lantern hanging from the leafy hem, a vine and buttress roots. Colours are the grey-tan bark, gold window and green vine from Rainroot cell 1-4.
rr-kapok-nook.name: partial
rr-kapok-nook.notes: The green top reads as a scalloped band of moss or grass on a block more than a tree canopy, so a stranger may call it a 'mossy stump house' or 'little hut' rather than a kapok tree. The round tab can look like a stem knob. At 36 px the window and lantern are only a few pixels. The script is at /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/rr-kapok-nook.py; it wrote rr-kapok-nook.png, rr-kapok-nook-36.png and rr-kapok-nook-preview.png in /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ after 2 renders. Both PNGs passed the kit check: exact sizes, alpha only 0 or 255, no pure black, 22 colours at 64 px and 21 at 36 px.

rr-hammock-hush.concept: A sloth clinging to a rope-bridge plank: the flat top side is the wooden plank (rope wraps, vine leaf, cream claws hooked over it), keyhole blanks cut into its left and right flanks below the raised arms, and a keyhole tab at the bottom is its dangling furry rump; grey-brown fur, cream face mask and dark teardrop eye patches from cell 6-3.
rr-hammock-hush.name: pass
rr-hammock-hush.notes: The side blanks are deep, so the fur below them looks a little like a separate block (like trousers), and the bottom tab is small at 36 px. Output files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/rr-hammock-hush.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-hammock-hush.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-hammock-hush-36.png and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-hammock-hush-preview.png.

rr-mate-mumble.concept: A mate gourd that is an inner-TBTB peg piece. The top peg tab is the heaped green yerba with a silver straw (bombilla) sticking out of it, the bottom peg tab is the gourd's foot, and the two side peg blanks pinch in the gourd's waist. It has a cream rim, a brown gourd body with a face, and a belly band painted as green hill terraces with tan paths, taken from cell 9-4.
rr-mate-mumble.name: partial
rr-mate-mumble.notes: Without the name, a stranger may see a cup or pot with a straw rather than a mate gourd. At 36 px the square yerba peg can look like a little green hat, and the foot peg can make the whole shape read slightly like a spinning top. The terrace greens and llama-cream rim match the cell, but the llama itself is not shown. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/rr-mate-mumble.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-mate-mumble.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-mate-mumble-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-mate-mumble-preview.png.

rr-bromeliad-bolt.concept: A spiky bromeliad rosette that is an inner-TTTT piece: all four tri tabs are plant parts (green leaf points W and E, a red flower-spike 'bolt' N, a bark root foot S), with straight sides between them, red-tipped strap leaves breaking up through the top edge, and pink bracts holding a blue cup of rain; colours are cell 1-1 leaf greens and bark brown plus the picture's heliconia red and river blue.
rr-bromeliad-bolt.name: partial
rr-bromeliad-bolt.notes: It clearly reads as a spiky leafy plant with a water cup, but a stranger might say pineapple top or agave rather than bromeliad. The cell is mostly tan tree bark, and that bark only shows in the small root foot.

rr-highland-ring.concept: A leafy canopy wreath-hoop made from the cell's greens: a rounded-square inner piece with round blanks on all four sides (inner-BBBB, round knob), a clear hole through the middle, a bark-wood ring wrapped in leaves, a brown branch twining round it, frosty cloud caps on the two top corners, and felt eyes either side of the bottom blank.
rr-highland-ring.name: partial
rr-highland-ring.notes: A stranger would most likely say "a snowy leaf wreath or hoop", not a highland ring, so the "highland, highest" idea rests only on the snow-cloud caps. The wood hoop and leaf wraps are hard to make out at 36 px, so at that size it reads mainly as a green ring-shaped puzzle piece.

rr-glimmer-frog.concept: A squat front-facing frog whose body is the puzzle piece (whimsy-frog). Its eyes sit on domes at the top corners. A hook tab on the east side is a curled front arm, a smaller hook tab rises on the north between the eyes, and a hook blank bites into the west flank. It is foliage green from the cell, its belly glows gold like the cell's lit window (#f5cf6a), and it sits on a strip of tan bark from the trunk.
rr-glimmer-frog.name: pass
rr-glimmer-frog.notes: The link to the picture rests on colour (leaf greens, the gold glowing window as the belly, the bark ledge); there is no frog in the Rainroot picture, so the motif is only borrowed. The east hook tab is a thin loop that reads as a stick arm. At 36 px the north hook between the eyes is a tiny ring, and the gold glimmer spots almost disappear. Script: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/rr-glimmer-frog.py. Output: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-glimmer-frog.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-glimmer-frog-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/rr-glimmer-frog-preview.png. Checks pass on both files: 15 colours, alpha only 0 or 255, no pure black. It took 3 renders.

mm-toadstool-tuck.concept: A red fly-agaric toadstool that is a corner piece. Its spotted red cap forms the domed top of the silhouette. The left side and the mossy turf bottom are flat. A round blank cuts into the cap top, and a second round blank on the right side under the brim exposes the cream stem, which carries the felt face. The olive moss, heather tufts and brown bud are taken from the Mistmoor cell.
mm-toadstool-tuck.name: pass
mm-toadstool-tuck.notes: The mushroom's silhouette still comes mostly from the domed cap. Its lower half is a square block of moss, so the stem does not show in the outline, and that part leans toward 'a piece with a painted stem'. The top blank in the cap can also read a little like a bite out of the cap. Files are in /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mm-toadstool-tuck.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-toadstool-tuck{,-36,-preview}.png.

mm-skerry-seal.concept: A plump grey harbour seal sits upright on its skerry (edge-TBB, keyhole). The flat S side is the grassy rock with heather dots. The keyhole tab on N is its raised snout balancing a buoy ball striped red and white like the lighthouse. Keyhole blanks on W and E bite into its flanks. The colours are the cell's sea-grey, lighthouse white and red, moor green and heather purple.
mm-skerry-seal.name: partial
mm-skerry-seal.notes: The seal reads mainly from its grey colour, pale belly, whiskers and the ball on its nose. The square body with rounded shoulders could also be taken for a hippo or a grey blob. The folded fore-flippers barely show, at 64 px or at 36 px, and I hit the limit of four renders before I could fix them. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mm-skerry-seal.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-skerry-seal.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-skerry-seal-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-skerry-seal-preview.png.

mm-peat-sip.concept: Peat Sip is the cottage's grey stone chimney stack drawn as an inner-TBBB peg piece. The peg tab on top is the terracotta chimney pot, with a puff of peat smoke beside it. The W, E and S peg blanks are cut into coursed stone with mortar lines. It has an arched amber hearth-glow mouth and moss and heather tufts at its foot. Colours are sampled from Mistmoor cell 8-5: stone #9c9d97, mortar #757670, amber #f2b84a/#d98a2b, heather #8a5a8e.
mm-peat-sip.name: partial
mm-peat-sip.notes: With the name covered, the chimney could be taken for a stone tower or a little castle. The pot and the smoke are the only chimney cues, and the smoke cloud floats as a separate island. The cell's lit amber window shows up only as the hearth glow in the mouth, so the picture match rests mostly on the grey stone and the heather.

mm-stone-sentry.concept: A mossy mistmoor headstone (a round-topped grey menhir) as an inner-TTTT tri piece. N tab: a moss tuft rising from the green moss cap. E and W tabs: stubby stone arms. S tab: a stone foot in a grass tuft. It has lichen spots, a crack, and the cell's grey stone and moss-green colours, with a stubborn flat stare.
mm-stone-sentry.name: partial
mm-stone-sentry.notes: The four pointed tri tabs read a little like compass arrows. Together with the thick moss cap and the top tuft, the head can look like an acorn or bush. A stranger would likely say "mossy rock" or "stone creature" but might not say headstone. The 36 px version keeps the silhouette, but the lichen and crack get thin. Script: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mm-stone-sentry.py. Checks pass: 14 and 12 colours, alpha only 0 or 255, no pure black.

ow-net-nudge.concept: Net Nudge is a bundled teal fishing net bag shaped as a corner-TB piece. The west and south sides are flat, so it sits on the quay on a rope band. The bag's top is gathered into a rope tie, and the round tab on top is a red-and-white buoy, using the gnome-hat red from cell 3-6. A round blank is cut into the east side. Dark cords fan down the net, and it has a felt face and a small silver fish.
ow-net-nudge.name: partial
ow-net-nudge.notes: The fanned cords and the sagging rows can also read as a tent, an umbrella or a jellyfish, so "fishing net" is not certain without the buoy as a hint. The tiny fish is lost at 36 px. The colours match the teal net and the gnome-hat red from Olivewhistle, but this cell is mostly the red gnome hat, so the net motif comes from the whole picture rather than from the cell. Both PNGs are the right size, use only alpha 0 or 255, have no pure black and use 19 and 18 colours.

mm-kite-knot.concept: A diamond kite that is an inner-TTBB piece tilted 45 degrees. Two small hook blanks bite the short upper edges and two curly hook tabs hang off the long lower edges. Purple and gold quadrants with brown cross spars come from cell 5-0, the face sits below the crossbar, and a bowed tail trails from the bottom tip.
mm-kite-knot.name: pass
mm-kite-knot.notes: The piece is tilted 45 degrees, so at 36 px the hook tabs and blanks read more as curls and notches than as a classic jigsaw outline, and the whole shape leans star-like. At 36 px the eyes also crowd the vertical spar. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/mm-kite-knot.py, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-kite-knot.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-kite-knot-36.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/mm-kite-knot-preview.png

ow-olive-pip.concept: A plump green olive that is an edge piece. The flat bottom side sits on a strip of ochre earth with a terracotta furrow, taken from the grove ground in cell 8-4. The north tab is a bark-brown twig with two pointed olive leaves on a double knob. The west tab is a small darker sister olive bulging out as a double tab, and the east side has a double blank bitten into the flesh.
ow-olive-pip.name: partial
ow-olive-pip.notes: With the name covered it reads as a green fruit or sprout with leaves, and a stranger might say pear or seedling before olive. The north leaves also lose the double-knob look. The link to the picture is only the olive green, the ochre and terracotta soil band, and the leaves; the cell's main motif, a white goat, is not used.

ow-jar-hum.concept: An ochre olive-oil amphora (a round belly clipped flat at top and bottom) that is also an inner-TBTB peg piece. The top peg tab is the jar's neck and terracotta lip, the bottom peg tab is its foot, and peg blanks cut into the left and right shoulders. It has terracotta loop handles, a terracotta shoulder band with a cream wave and an olive sprig on the belly, all in the cell 8-7 colours (ochre jar #d8a854, terracotta pot #c7643a, cream wall). Its face is happy, with an open humming mouth.
ow-jar-hum.name: partial
ow-jar-hum.notes: It reads as a round pot or urn more than an amphora: the flat-topped belly and the over-the-top handles can look like a basket or pot handle, especially at 36 px. The jar idea holds, but a stranger might say "pot" or "basket" before "oil jar". Files are /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ow-jar-hum.py and the outputs /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/ow-jar-hum.png, ow-jar-hum-36.png and ow-jar-hum-preview.png. Checks pass: 14 and 11 colours, alpha only 0 or 255, no pure black.

ow-sun-glint.concept: A setting sun that is itself an inner-TTTT piece. The body is a gold rounded square, and its four tri tabs on short necks are the sun's rays: orange on the top, left and right, and a sea-blue reflection streak on the bottom. The lower body sinks into a sea band with white glint dashes, and a plum island hump sits on the horizon. Colours come from cell 2-2 (pale sunset gold, plum island, sea blue). A white twinkle and a winking face match the blurb.
ow-sun-glint.name: partial
ow-sun-glint.notes: The square core and four pointed tri tabs make a symmetric four-point-star outline, so without the face and sea it could read as a star or compass more than a round sun. At 36 px the tab necks nearly merge into the heads. There are no blanks to show because the shape is TTTT. Files are at /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ow-sun-glint.py, and ow-sun-glint.png, ow-sun-glint-36.png and ow-sun-glint-preview.png in /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/.

ow-press-ring.concept: The Olivewhistle olive-press millstone (cell 6-5) is a grey speckled stone wheel with a brown rim, drawn as a rounded-square piece with a double blank in each of its four sides (inner-BBBB, double). It has a dark wooden axle hub holding a green olive, a ring of golden oil around the hub with a drip below it, and a felt face on the upper stone.
ow-press-ring.name: partial
ow-press-ring.notes: The silhouette reads clearly as a puzzle piece, but the four blanks give it a cross-like outline that hides the round wheel. A stranger would likely say "stone wheel" or "millstone" rather than "olive press". The oil ring is what tells you what it does, and at 36 px it shrinks to a thin gold arc. Script: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/ow-press-ring.py. ow-harbour-leap.concept: A fat grey dolphin leaping out of a blue harbour block, built as one whimsy-dolphin piece. Its back, fin, beak and flukes form the top of the outline, and a cream foam waterline crosses it with blue sea below. Hook tabs stick out on the E and S sides, and a hook blank cuts into the W side under the beak. The grey, sea blue and breakwater cream are sampled from cell 4-4.
ow-harbour-leap.name: pass
ow-harbour-leap.notes: At 36 px the hook tabs are thin, so the outline reads more as a dolphin on a block than as a clear jigsaw piece. The E hook and the W blank show, but the S tab looks like a stubby stalk. The dolphin also looks blocky and squat rather than mid-leap, because the square core flattens its curve.

bb-slushbelly.concept: A snowman from Birchbramble cell 8-6 whose snow body is a corner piece. The brown top hat's flat crown is the flat top side and the left side is flat. Round blanks cut the right side (a melted scoop out of the belly) and the bottom (into a slushy blue puddle on a grass edge). It has the cell's red scarf and carrot nose.
bb-slushbelly.name: partial
bb-slushbelly.notes: The snow body is still a square block, so the snowman mostly comes from the hat, scarf, carrot nose and the faint head contour, not from a two-ball outline. At 36 px it can read as a snowy piece wearing a hat rather than clearly as a snowman. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/bb-slushbelly.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/bb-slushbelly.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/bb-slushbelly-36.png and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/bb-slushbelly-preview.png (2 renders, 24 colours, hard alpha, no black pixels).

bb-gander-gait.concept: Slate-grey goose walking left as an edge piece: flat bottom = grass strip with orange feet; top keyhole tab stretched into the long neck and round head with an orange beak; right keyhole tab = tail tuft under a folded dark wing; left keyhole blank cut into the breast; grey, orange and grass green from cell 1-7.
bb-gander-gait.name: pass
bb-gander-gait.notes: The keyhole knob style hardly shows: the tail tab and breast blank read as plain rounded knobs or slots rather than keyholes. The neck is a custom stretched tab, so the head tab no longer has the exact keyhole profile.

bb-catkin-crown.concept: A stout chunk of white birch trunk with dark bark dashes, wearing a leafy green crown, drawn as an inner-TTTT piece with double knobs: the top tab is two leaf lobes with a gold bud, the side tabs are gold-brown catkin bunches hanging from the crown, and the bottom tab is two bark root-feet. Colours are birch white, catkin brown and gold, and birch-leaf green, all from cell 10-1.
bb-catkin-crown.name: partial
bb-catkin-crown.notes: The white body with a green top can still read as a turnip or radish before it reads as a birch, even with the bark dashes. The banded catkin tabs look more like wicker bundles than hanging catkins. Only 2 of the 4 allowed renders were used, so another pass could fix this.

bb-samovar-puff.concept: A brass samovar whose square urn body is an inner-TBBB peg piece. The N peg tab is the chimney, with a blue cap and a curl of steam. Peg blanks W and E cut in under short shoulder handles, and the S peg blank splits the foot in two. It has a blue domed lid, a red kerchief band with cream dots and a red tap, all in colours from the Birchbramble porch samovar and the doll in cell 9-4.
bb-samovar-puff.name: partial
bb-samovar-puff.notes: The urn shape is still quite square and the side blanks make a waist. A stranger might say "a teapot or kettle pal" or "a brass jar" before "samovar". The chimney, steam and tap carry the idea, but at 36 px the tap almost disappears. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/bb-samovar-puff.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/bb-samovar-puff{,-36,-preview}.png. Both sizes pass the checks: exactly 64 and 36 px, alpha only 0 or 255, 18 colours, no pure black. It took 3 renders.

bb-homing-stork.concept: A white stork flying side-on and facing left. Its square body and wing are the piece core, with tri tabs on the north side (a raised wing tip with a black tip) and the south side (black flight feathers), and a tri blank cut into the east side as a notched tail. The neck, head and red beak break out to the west, red legs trail out the lower right, and a sky-blue bundle with a cloud-white knot hangs from the beak. The colours come from cell 6-0 (sky #9ccbe5 and cloud white) and from the picture's white storks with red beaks.
bb-homing-stork.name: pass
bb-homing-stork.notes: The stork carrying a bundle matches the picture's storks, but the sky blue from the cell appears only in the small bundle, so the pal is mostly white, black and red. At 36 px the beak shrinks to a few red pixels, so the head relies on its neck curve to read.

bb-chimney-nest.concept: A white brick chimney stack topped by a big twig nest with a white stork sitting in it (slate wing tips, red beak looking left). It is an inner-BBBB keyhole piece: the N blank is the nest's cup, the W and E blanks bite into the sides of the nest, and the S blank is the chimney's fire-hole arch. Twig brown, chimney cream and stork white/slate are sampled from cell 7-1.
bb-chimney-nest.name: partial
bb-chimney-nest.notes: The stork reads clearly, but the nest is a flat brown slab with line twigs and not a rounded woven bowl, and the S blank makes the chimney base look a little like two legs. At 36 px the stork head is tiny, and the piece reads more as "a bird on a brown block" than as a chimney nest. dw-sherbet-sip.concept: A mint-tea pot that is also a corner-TT piece. The left and bottom sides are flat, with a brass foot along the bottom. A round tab on top is the brass lid finial and a round tab on the right is the brass handle. A brass spout curves up from the lower left. The body is glazed in the cell's sunset (orange over coral) under a mauve lid, with a purple dune and an indigo camel silhouette along the bottom.
dw-sherbet-sip.name: pass
dw-sherbet-sip.notes: The body is a square block, so the pot reads as a teapot mainly because of the spout, the finial and the handle, not its shape. It looks more like a tea tin than a bulbous Moroccan pot. Corner-TT has no blanks, so the piece reads only from the two round tabs and the flat sides. The camel is small and only roughly readable at 36 px. Files: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/dw-sherbet-sip.py and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/dw-sherbet-sip.png, dw-sherbet-sip-36.png, dw-sherbet-sip-preview.png (both sizes have 19 colours, hard alpha, no pure black).

dw-scarab-roll.concept: Top-down scarab beetle as an edge-BTB keyhole piece: the keyhole tab on top is the head on its neck (toothed front, clubbed antennae, felt face), keyhole blanks left and right bite into the teal wing cases, and the flat bottom is the back end holding a sand ball. Colours from cell 3-7: turquoise stripe, lamp gold/orange, rug-red rim, the rug's gold diamonds on the shell, sand ball.
dw-scarab-roll.name: partial
dw-scarab-roll.notes: Reads as a beetle or bug, not clearly a scarab rolling a ball. The sand ball sits inside the shell as a round tan patch that can look like a cookie or belly mark, and the yellow head with antennae is slightly bee-like.

dw-canyon-crown.concept: A rose-red sandstone mesa shaped as an inner-TTTT piece with tri knobs. The north tri tab is the crown's middle spire, with a gold lantern-glow jewel, set between two craggy cliff pinnacles. The east and west tri tabs are plum rock ledges and the south tri tab is a dusk-purple scree foot. The body has stepped strata ledges, a purple dusk base and a dark cave mouth, all in the colours of cell 1-2 (#b7525a rose, #893a50 plum, #7b4581 dusk, #da7a6a glow, #3b2440 doorway).
dw-canyon-crown.name: partial
dw-canyon-crown.notes: The crown comes through clearly, but a stranger would probably say 'a rock with a crown' or 'a crown block' rather than 'a canyon mesa'. At 36 px the two side pinnacles can also look a little like cat ears. The four tri tabs read as spiky points more than as classic jigsaw knobs, though the neck-and-tab rhythm on all four sides still says 'puzzle piece'. The script is /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/scripts/dw-canyon-crown.py and the outputs are /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/dw-canyon-crown.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/dw-canyon-crown-36.png and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/dw-canyon-crown-preview.png (17 colours, alpha only 0 or 255, no pure black).

dw-lantern-lark.concept: A plump crested lark whose body is a round-cornered inner piece (inner-TBBB with peg knobs): the right-side peg tab is its orange beak, and the top, left and bottom sides are peg blanks. It uses the indigo, violet, rose and pink sunset colours of cell 5-2, plus a string of yellow lanterns from the picture draped across its breast.
dw-lantern-lark.name: pass
dw-lantern-lark.notes: The weak point is how much it reads as a puzzle piece. The beak tab and the top notch are clear at 36 px. But the tail, crest and dark wing break up the outline on the left, so the left and bottom blanks are hard to pick out and the square core reads only partly. Both PNGs pass the checks: no black pixels, alpha only 0 or 255, 19 and 18 colours.

dw-oasis-hoop.concept: A coral-and-cream life-ring swim float that is also an inner-BBBB piece: a rounded square ring with a double blank cut into the middle of all four sides. The hole shows the cell's purple oasis pool with pink and orange sunset reflection streaks, and a felt face peeks out of the water there. It wears a lily pad from the cell as a hat and holds a brown date in the lower-left corner (the "keeps a date" blurb).
dw-oasis-hoop.name: pass
dw-oasis-hoop.notes: The face sits on the purple pool inside the hole, not on the ring. It can read as a small purple creature inside a float rather than the float being the creature. At 36 px the date in the lower-left corner shrinks to a small brown lump. dw-mirage-moon.concept: A fat cream crescent moon opening to the right is the whole piece: keyhole tab out of its round back (W), keyhole blank cut into its lower-left belly, sleepy felt face on the thick back, purple night-cloud wisp from cell 0-0 on the lower horn and a gold star by the upper tip.
dw-mirage-moon.name: pass
dw-mirage-moon.notes: The moon wins over the piece: with only two knobs on the curved back and a soft keyhole shape at 36 px, it reads first as a smiling crescent and only second as a jigsaw piece. The cell's deep purple sky shows up only as the small cloud wisp, so the link to the picture is weaker than the colours alone suggest.

gc-calabash-cup.concept: A half-gourd calabash cup full of rain water, seen from the front. It is a corner-BB piece. The rim (with blue water inside) and the left side are the two flat sides. Round blanks cut into the right side and into the bowl's foot at the bottom, and the bottom corners are rounded so the shape reads as a bowl. Colours come from cell 1-5: plank-brown gourd with dark bowed ribs from the wooden door, a thatch-gold lip from the eaves, a rain-blue surface, and a vine stem and leaf from the canopy.
gc-calabash-cup.name: partial
gc-calabash-cup.notes: Without the name, it reads as a smiling wooden cup or bowl of water, but it could also be taken for a bucket or a tree stump, so "calabash" is not obvious. The bottom blank, between the two converging ribs, still looks a little like two stubby legs, especially at 36 px. gc-drum-tap.concept: A djembe drum pal woven from straw, with a cream drumhead, red rim and a deep-red foot. The bottom side is flat, the double tab on top is two red-headed mallets resting on the drumhead, and double blanks on the left and right sides pinch in the djembe waist. Its gold body has the brown slat rows of the pavilion thatch from cell 4-3, and the red comes from the picture's drum.
gc-drum-tap.name: partial
gc-drum-tap.notes: The double-tab mallet heads still look a bit like a heart or a red mushroom cap, especially at 36 px. The oval drumhead and pinched waist give a drum or cake-like hourglass read, but a stranger might call it a cake or stool before a drum. gc-yam-nub.concept: A plump, knobbly yam that is itself an inner-TBTB peg piece. The N peg tab is a green sprout stalk with two leaves, the S peg tab is a stubby root tail, and square peg blanks bite into the E and W flanks. The skin is the clay-path red-brown of cell 5-6, with curved growth rings, dimples and root hairs; a grass-green tuft sits at its foot and a nicked orange nub shows on top. It has a giggling face.
gc-yam-nub.name: partial
gc-yam-nub.notes: It clearly reads as a sprouting root vegetable, but not necessarily as a yam: a stranger could say potato, beet or a clay lump. The body is still fairly square, because the corners need to stay square for the piece to read. At 36 px the growth rings are faint, so the sprout and the colour carry most of the idea. gc-shellstep.concept: A tortoise seen from above. Its rounded-square olive shell is the piece body, with gold rim scutes, umber seams and a pale centre scute, all taken from the tortoise in cell 9-6. The four double tabs are the tortoise's parts: N is the head, whose two lobes hold the eyes; E and W are the paired legs with cream claws; S is the stubby tail. The skin is the picture's grey-brown.
gc-shellstep.name: pass
gc-shellstep.notes: Three renders done; sizes are 64 and 36 px, alpha is only 0 or 255, there is no pure black, and each size uses 12 or 13 colours. Squint test: the shape is inner-TTTT, so it has no blanks. Its puzzle read comes from four double tabs on a square body, and at 36 px those tabs are clear but no blank is visible. Weakest point: the side double tabs have narrow necks, so at 36 px they still look a bit like bone ends rather than legs. Also, the larger 36 px head made little visible difference. Outputs: /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/gc-shellstep.png, /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/gc-shellstep-36.png and /home/user/gnome-venture/art-review/redo/out/gc-shellstep-preview.png.

gc-canopy-loop.concept: A brown canopy monkey whose body is the inner piece with four keyhole blanks (one on each side). The four corner lobes are two raised arms gripping green leaf tufts and two tan feet. The face sits in the centre, a rainbow scarf crosses the chest and a looped tail curls off the lower right. Bridge-wood browns, rainbow bands and canopy green come from cell 5-1.
gc-canopy-loop.name: pass
gc-canopy-loop.notes: The cell's rainbow and bridge wood show up only as the scarf and the fur colour, and the scarf's ends on the leg lobes can read as rainbow shorts. At 36 px the face is small (about 6 px), so the monkey reading leans on the ears-like leaf hands and the tail loop. gc-parrot-pennant.concept: A green parrot with a red cap, sitting on a perch. Its square body is the piece: the east hook tab is a cream hooked beak, the north hook tab is a red-and-yellow crest knob, and a hook blank bites into its back on the west. The wing is leaf green with brown veins like the 0-6 leaf cell, and the picture's yellow, red and blue bunting pennants hang from the perch.
gc-parrot-pennant.name: partial
gc-parrot-pennant.notes: The beak hook only half reads as a hooked parrot beak (at 36 px it can look like a cream club). The bird's body is very boxy, so without the beak and tail it could pass for a green bird in general. The pennants and the green-and-brown leaf colours come from the picture, but the picture's own parrots are grey, so the match to the source is through the leaf cell and the bunting rather than the bird itself. th-coffee-crumb.concept: Coffee Crumb is a roasted coffee bean as a corner-TT piece with round knobs. The W and S sides are flat. The N tab is the round crown of its very large woven straw hat, whose brim droops past the right side. The E tab is a second roasted bean it holds out. The body has a bean crease in the shape of an S. The colours come from cell 7-7: basket-weave tan #d9a359 for the hat, grass green #6b9a3a for the hat band, dark roast wood #794a1e for the bean, and earth orange #cf8f2d for the crumbs.
th-coffee-crumb.name: partial
th-coffee-crumb.notes: The square brown body with a crease reads more like a stump or a coffee mug (the E tab looks like a handle) than a coffee bean. The big straw hat reads, but the green band on the crown's narrow neck looks a little like an acorn stem. The link to the picture rests only on the colours: the tan basket weave, the green and the dark wood. The cell's woven basket of grains is not a strong motif here. th-flamingo-flick.concept: A pink flamingo shaped as an edge-BTB piece. The flat bottom is the waterhole (blue water over orange sand, with one leg standing in it). The top keyhole tab is the flared neck and round head, with a cream beak that has a dark tip. Keyhole blanks are cut into the fluffy body on the left and right. The pink, sky blue and sand colours come from cell 3-7.
th-flamingo-flick.name: pass
th-flamingo-flick.notes: At 36 px the head and eye are tiny, so the flamingo reads mostly from the beak and the pink colour. The body above the blanks flares into wing-like shoulders, which could read as outstretched wings rather than a folded bird. th-acacia-antler.name: partial
th-acacia-antler.notes: The antlers, the flat-topped acacia pads and the hanging nests carry the idea, but the body is a square box with a deer nose. A stranger would probably say "a tree-antlered deer" or "a little tree spirit" rather than name the acacia stag exactly. The inner-TTTT shape has no blanks, so only tabs show at 36 px. th-termite-tower.concept: A tapered terracotta termite mound with a felt face, with mud-brick courses and green and gold grass tufts at its foot, taken from Thornacre cell 0-6. The top side is a round tab that forms the mound's dark wet spire tip. The left, right and bottom sides are round blanks cut into the lower half of the mound.
th-termite-tower.name: partial
th-termite-tower.notes: The three blanks sit close together in the narrow base, so the lower half reads somewhat as two stubby legs (pilot failure mode 5). The cone with a knob on top could also be taken for a bell rather than a termite mound. The faint brick dashes at 36 px are the main mound cue. I used all 4 renders, so these issues were not fixed. th-tall-tiptoe.concept: A giraffe facing right whose square torso is the puzzle piece: the tail tuft on the left is a double tab, a double blank is cut into the chest under the neck, and another double blank between the legs turns the bottom into two legs. The two ossicones are drawn by hand and are not the kit's double-knob tab, so the top side reads more as giraffe than as a puzzle tab. th-kopje-keeper.concept: The sage-green soapstone bird statue on its plinth from cell 1-2, drawn as an inner-TTBB hook piece. br-petal-pinch.concept: A small cherry-blossom tree shaped as a corner piece. Its square pink canopy has puffy bumps along the top and right edges, and two blossom-puff round tabs stick out north and east. The west and south sides are flat. br-petal-pinch.notes: The tree is only shown by paint in the lower third (sky band, trunk, grass) inside a square outline, so it is close to 'a picture on a piece'. Brown and cream striped forewings sit over red-orange hindwings with a cream band and blue eyespots, on a mossy green strip taken from the cell and picture.
pl-tgm-1.name: pass
pl-tgm-1.notes: The wings still fill a plain rectangle and only the head and antennae break the outline, so it leans a little towards 'piece with a moth painted on'. The cell's teal and pillar show only as the moss strip at the bottom; most of the colour comes from the picture's moth.

pl-tgm-2.concept: A cream prayer-flag cloth hung on a straight green bamboo pole (flat W side, gold finial); double tab E is the fluttering tail with a teal hem, double tab S is the teal tassels, double blank N; diagonal tan/umber moth-wing band and moon cream, bamboo green and teal from cell 7-1; nervous face with a sweat drop.
pl-tgm-2.name: partial
pl-tgm-2.notes: The diagonal moth-wing band slightly overlaps the mouth and reads more like a sash or stick than a wing pattern, and the plain cream cloth reads as a generic flag more than a prayer flag.

pl-tgm-3.concept: Temple Chip is a stepped sandstone temple block (a little ziggurat) built as an inner-TBBB peg piece. The N peg tab is the shrine capstone on the top step, and square peg blanks are cut into the W, E and S sides of the wide base course. The face sits in the slate window niche with the orange L glyph from cell 7-5, on speckled sandstone #b8a47a with a slate mortar line.
pl-tgm-3.name: partial
pl-tgm-3.notes: The S blank between two base blocks still reads a bit like legs, so it can pass for a stone robot or golem as easily as a temple stone. Strangers would probably say 'stepped stone block or pyramid' rather than name a temple step for certain. At 36 px the orange glyph shrinks to a short mouth-like bar. pl-tgm-4.concept: A tiger moth seen from above, its spread wings forming the square body of an inner-TTTT piece. It has four tri tabs: the furry head with antennae at the top, the brown forewing tips at the sides, and the striped abdomen tip at the bottom. The forewings have cream and brown tiger stripes in a V, and the hindwings are red with orange and blue eye-spots, all taken from the source picture and the cell's red, cream and brown.
pl-tgm-4.name: pass
pl-tgm-4.notes: The shape is inner-TTTT, so there is no blank to see, and at 36 px the tri tabs are small next to the wide body, which makes the piece read less strongly than the moth. pl-tgm-6.concept: A front-facing tiger moth whose spread wings make a near-square whimsy piece. Its two curled slate antennae are the top hook tabs, the left forewing has a hook tab, and there are hook blanks in the right hindwing and between the hindwing lobes. Brown and cream striped forewings and red-orange hindwings with gold-rimmed blue eyespot lockets come from the picture; the stone-tan body and gold rims echo the temple window in the cell.
pl-tgm-6.name: pass
pl-tgm-6.notes: The palette and motif follow the whole picture (the moth), but the cell is mostly temple stone with a gold window, and only the body and the gold locket rims carry that; the dark slate in the antennae is also the window frame colour. The left hook tab is small and muddy at 36 px, so the right blank and the bottom gap do most of the work of saying 'puzzle piece'.

pl-scr-1.concept: A tiny sandstone pyramid (corner-BB, hook). The two flat sides are the base, which sits in the mauve dune, and the small gold top that waits for its capstone. A hook blank is bitten into each sloping face. Colours are the cream sunset sky and mauve dune from cell 1-4 plus the tomb's sandstone tan, with stone-block joints and a felt face low on the front.
pl-scr-1.name: pass
pl-scr-1.notes: It reads as a pyramid right away, but the puzzle-piece read is weaker. A triangle with two comma bites does not have the square core of a normal piece, and at 36 px the hook blanks look like small notches that leave thin lower flaps a little like feet.

pl-scr-2.concept: A teal scarab seen from above that is also an edge-TBB piece with peg knobs. The flat bottom side is a sandstone plinth with mauve slots, taken from the obelisk in cell 3-5. The peg tab on top is the beetle's head, with gold clypeus teeth. The two peg blanks cut into the waist between the pronotum and the wing cases. The shell has a gold seam and dotted gold lines, and three pairs of slate legs.
pl-scr-2.name: partial
pl-scr-2.notes: The peg-shaped head is square, so it can read as a little hat or chimney. Without the six legs the creature could pass for a teal robot, not a scarab. The cell's mauve appears only as the dark plinth slots, so the picture link rests on the scarab's teal and gold and the sandstone base.

pl-scr-3.concept: Dune Ticktock is an hourglass drawn as an inner-TBTB double-knob piece. The top and bottom tabs are the twin finials on the mauve caps (the colour is the cell 0-5 dusk sky, #a8587a). The double blanks on the left and right pinch the glass into the hourglass waist. Dune-gold sand drains from a funnel in the top bulb, which carries the face, into a pile below.
pl-scr-3.name: pass
pl-scr-3.notes: The source cell is plain mauve sky, so the only link to the picture is colour: mauve caps and dune-gold sand. Nothing in the drawing shows the scarab or the tomb. At 36 px the face on the top sand is tiny and the eyes nearly merge, but the hourglass and the piece still read from the outline. pl-scr-4.concept: Teal sand scarab seen from above, inner-TTTT with tri knobs: its rounded square shell is the piece. The N tab is the pointed slate head, the E and W tabs are mid legs with pointed feet, and the S tab is the tail tip. Short bent slate front and hind legs at the corners make six legs. pl-scr-6.concept: A sandstone-and-faience scarab charm seen from above that is also the piece. Its domed teal wing cases with straight E/W sides form the piece body, the E foreleg is a double tab, a double blank is cut into the W side, and a double blank at S ends the wing-case seam. It has a carved sandstone pronotum (the cell's tomb-wall tans and grooves), a dark umber head with felt eyes, four brown legs and a red jewel set at the top of the seam (the picture's teal scarab and the blurb's red jewel).
pl-scr-6.name: partial
pl-scr-6.notes: The legs and teal wing cases make it read as a beetle or bug, but the broad sandstone pronotum and round dark head with its two eyes still look a bit like a frog or mole face, so "scarab" specifically is not certain without the name. The teal comes from the picture's beetle rather than the cell, which is all sandstone tans; only the pronotum, trim and grooves carry the cell's palette. I stopped at the 4-render limit. pl-ana-2.concept: A green anaconda coiled into a square edge piece, lying on a strip of bark. The flat south side is a tan, mossy bark branch taken from cell 3-5. The west tri tab is the pointed tail tip, the north tri blank is a V-shaped bite out of the top coil, and the east tri tab is the snake's triangular head with an eye and a red forked tongue. The greens and dark spots come from the snake in the picture.
pl-ana-2.name: partial
pl-ana-2.notes: The snake reads clearly from the head, but the body below it does not. The three coils look more like stacked green layers (a cake or a hedge) than a coiled snake, even after rounding the coil ends and adding umber grooves. Its colours come from the doorway in cell 6-5: plum body, the door's gold lantern dots as spots and a light sill belly, plus a teal creek band and a burped bubble from the picture's stream.

pl-ana-3.notes: A stranger may call it a generic plum monster rather than a frog. The tall eye bumps and the deep N blank give it an H-shaped, two-tower head, and the wide mouth and webbed toes are weak cues at 36 px. pl-bvd-1.concept: A beaver sitting face-on is the corner-BB piece. Its flat west and south sides are its back and its seat on the lodge floor. The gnawed-stick tab on the north side is the weakest cue: at 36 px it reads as a generic peg rather than a stick. pl-bvd-3.concept: Tunnel Trickle is a pond-blue water drop that is also an inner-TBTB piece. Its N tri tab is the drop's pointed tip, its S tri tab is a drip falling off its round bottom, and tri blanks cut into the E and W sides. A tan beaver-dam log with a dark ring end, taken from cell 2-7, runs across its belly as the tunnel it trickles through. The colours are the cell's pond blues and log tans.
pl-bvd-3.name: partial
pl-bvd-3.notes: Because the shoulders slope in toward the tip, the upper half reads a little like a spade or diamond as much as a water drop. A stranger would probably say "water drop on a log", but they might also say "blue spade creature". The 36 px version keeps the tab and blanks but loses the drop's shine and most of the log grain.

pl-bvd-4.concept: Damwall Logs, three stubby dam logs piled a little crooked into a square inner-TTTT piece. Each double tab is a pair of stick ends poking out of the pile, each with a cut end. The logs have rounded ends and the middle log shows its sawn end grain. The colours come from cell 1-5: bark browns, tan end grain, dark plum gaps between logs and a strip of river blue lapping the bottom log. The felt face sits on the middle log.
pl-bvd-4.name: pass
pl-bvd-4.notes: The double tabs still look a bit like bone ends rather than clearly sticks, and the inner-TTTT shape has no blanks, so the piece reads only from its tabs. The end-grain faces on the logs are narrow and their rings are hard to see at 36 px. pl-bvd-5.concept: A stick-and-mud beaver lodge that is an inner-BBBB piece with round blanks on all four sides. It has a domed top with short stick ends poking out, woven tan and brown stick bands taken from the cell, a dark arched door at a blue waterline, and a beaver peeking out of the door.

pl-ffy-1.concept: A firefly that is a corner-TT round piece. The west and south sides are flat, so it sits in the corner. The round north tab is its fuzzy brown head with two antennae that have glowing tips. The round east tab is a pale blue wing. The upper body is the brown fuzzy thorax with the face. The lower body is the glowing lemon lantern tail, ringed in cave-glow green and stitched with the cell's dotted rows.
pl-ffy-1.name: partial
pl-ffy-1.notes: The body is still a mostly square two-tone block, so the firefly comes mainly from the antennae, the wing tab and the glowing tail colours. A stranger might say "cute bug" or "jar bug" rather than "firefly", especially at 36 px. The north tab head also reads a little like a stem or knob.

pl-ffy-3.concept: A lake-blue firefly whose body is the piece (inner-TBTB, peg). The left and right peg tabs are pale glassy wings and the top and bottom peg blanks cut into the body, with two yellow-tipped antennae rising beside the top blank. The body uses the cave-lake blues from the 6-6 cell, with light ripple streaks over a green and yellow lantern belly.

pl-ffy-3.notes: The square peg wings look more like flat bars than firefly wings, and the bottom blank can read as two stubby legs, so a stranger may say "glowing beetle or bug" rather than "firefly". The idea that it is a reflection in the lake comes only from the blue water colours and faint ripple lines; nothing in the shape shows it.

The W and E double tabs are two pairs of pale ice-blue wings with brown shoulders and navy veins (four spare wings). The N double tab is the head bump, with spark-green antenna tips. pl-ffy-4.name: partial
pl-ffy-4.notes: The double-lobed side wings still read a little like bones or mitts rather than wings. A stranger might say "bug" or "bee" before "firefly". The N tab is the cream-gold crown of the fuzzy dome, the E and W tabs are pink bracts flaring sideways, and the S tab is a mauve-brown stem foot. pl-fyn-5.concept: A sleepy dusk sun peeking over a dark fynbos ridge through a gap in a square puff of purple and pink smoke. It is an inner-BBBB piece with a round blank cut into each of the four sides, softly rounded smoke-puff corners and two small puffs on the top edge. The colours come from the cell's smoke purples and pinks (#7a4a8c, #c0689c, #9d5994, #563c78) and the picture's sunset orange (#e8805a).

pl-fyn-5.notes: The sunset mostly lives in the paint rather than the outline: apart from the soft puff corners, the silhouette is a plain four-blank piece, which is close to the "piece with a picture on it" failure mode. Bigger puffs on the outline made the top read as ears or a bow, so I took them back out. At 36 px the sun is small, but its orange half-disc over the dark ridge still reads as a sunset. The N keyhole tab is the tallest feather with a dark flamingo tip. The E keyhole tab is the twine bow, and the W keyhole blank bites into the feather fan. The colours are the shallows pinks, the lilac water and the gold sun from cell 5-3, with chevron feather barbs and cream quills.
pl-wfla-2.name: partial
pl-wfla-2.notes: The bundle reads as tied pink feathers at 64 px, but a stranger could also call it a feather headdress or a pink brush, because the fan barely spreads past the square core. At 36 px the barbs are dropped and it relies on the pink stripes and cream quills. The twine bow tab is a plain gold nub, not a clear bow.

pl-wfla-4.concept: A pink flamingo that is itself an inner-TTTT jigsaw piece. The N tab is its long S-curved neck and head with the cream beak and dark bent tip. The S tab is two feet (a double knob) standing in the lavender shallows, the W tab is a darker tail tuft and the E tab is the puffed chest, both double knobs. Colours and motif come from cell 9-6: flamingo pink, lavender water and a cream ripple.
pl-wfla-4.name: pass
pl-wfla-4.notes: The N tab is a neck, head and beak rather than a true double knob, so the knob style holds only on three sides. Below the neck, the body is still a square piece with the wing and legs painted on. At 36 px the wing and ripple lines are faint and the flamingo read rests almost entirely on the neck and beak. pl-wpry-3.concept: A round, speckled sand pebble that is itself an inner-TBTB keyhole piece. The keyhole tabs at top and bottom are a small light cairn stone stacked on top and a nub it sits on, and keyhole blanks bite into the left and right flanks. A pebble also has no strong outline of its own, so the speckles and the flag string carry most of the idea. I used all 4 renders and did not fix the stalk-like top tab.
